extracted.intended_audience: extramural research community (researchers, research administrators, reviewers, small businesses, foreign applicants, NIH staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Central NIH landing page summarizing where to find funding opportunities, how to apply, process steps, policy and compliance resources, and role-specific guidance for applicants and recipients of NIH grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with the NIH Grants Policy Statement (NIHGPS)
rubrics_metrics.description: By accepting a grant award, recipients agree to comply with the requirements in the NIH Grants Policy Statement unless the notice of award states otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NIHGPS makes available, in a single document, the policy requirements that serve as the terms and conditions of NIH grant awards. Applicants and recipients should consult the NIHGPS for specific policy obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices of Policy Changes superseding NIHGPS
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices published in the NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts can supersede information in the NIH Grants Policy Statement and/or provide reminders to applicants and recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH incorporates these notices into the annual update of the NIH Grants Policy Statement. Applicants/recipients should monitor the NIH Guide for Grants and Contracts for current notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants process adherence (planning → submission → award → closeout)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants Process Overview: learn about the steps required for an application to proceed from planning and submission through award and closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow the defined process steps for successful submission, award management, and closeout; see the Grants Process Overview for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and institutional readiness to do business with NIH
rubrics_metrics.description: New to NIH: Gain an understanding of key concepts like how the NIH structure impacts funding and how to get registered to do business with us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should complete required registrations (institutional credentials, system accounts) and learn institutional requirements before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and oversight obligations for grant recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal requirements, guidelines and resources for the extramural community involving grants compliance are provided to assist the community in understanding compliance obligations of their grant award and the proper use of grant funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are expected to understand and meet federal compliance requirements and use grant funds appropriately; consult compliance and oversight resources for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research training and career development program eligibility and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Explore NIH funding programs that can support your research career, from the undergraduate level to the established investigator level and everything in between.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators at different career stages should identify programs appropriate to their career level and follow program-specific application requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch requirements (policy topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biosketch listed as a select policy topic relevant to applications and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Biosketch policy topic page for detailed formatting, content, and disclosure requirements for investigator biosketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Support disclosure requirements (policy topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Support listed as a select policy topic relevant to application and award management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Other Support policy topic for instructions on what to disclose about current and pending support and how to format those disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission timing and late submission policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Update of NIH Late Application Submission Policy and End of Continuous Submission (policy update referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow current NIH policies on application submission windows and late submission rules; recent updates may change continuous submission allowances—consult policy updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review practice standards and modifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuation of Modifications to Peer Review Practices (policy update referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH periodically updates peer review practices; applicants and reviewers should consult current guidance to understand review criteria and procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency Act subaward reporting applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicability of Transparency Act Subaward Reporting Requirements (policy update referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and recipients must determine applicability of subaward reporting requirements under the Transparency Act and follow reporting rules where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for basic experimental studies with humans
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of Changes for Basic Experimental Studies with Humans (policy update referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers conducting basic experimental studies with humans must follow updated NIH definitions and policy changes; consult the specific policy notice for procedural and compliance details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior approval requirements for changes to domestic subawards
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior Approval Requirement for Changes to Domestic Subawards (policy update referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may need NIH prior approval for certain changes to domestic subawards; check the policy notice for which changes require approval and the process to request it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmonization of 'intervention' definition with the Common Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmonizing the NIH Definition of Intervention with the Common Rule (policy update referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions affecting human subjects research are being aligned with regulatory requirements; investigators should review definitional changes to determine impacts on their studies and compliance needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing Plan Format Available (announcement referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants required to submit Data Management and Sharing Plans should follow the latest NIH-prescribed format, including pilot/formatted templates when provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and safety monitoring policy modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernizing NIH Data and Safety Monitoring Policy Webinar: NIH intends to modernize the approach to data and safety monitoring and is committed to engaging the public in development of an updated policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should be aware of forthcoming changes to data and safety monitoring expectations and engage with NIH guidance; monitor policy development and attend informational events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to previously funded research data and results (RePORT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Access reports, data, and analyses of NIH research activities, including information on NIH expenditures and the results of NIH-supported research, in the Research Portfolio Online Reporting Tools (RePORT) system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RePORT to examine prior funding patterns, project outcomes, and NIH expenditures when preparing applications or assessing the funding landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-specific guidance for applicants and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse by Role: tailored resources for Researchers, Research Administrators, Reviewers, Small Businesses, Foreign Applicants, Media and the Public, NIH Staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals should consult the role-specific pages for guidance, requirements, and contacts relevant to their role in the grants ecosystem.
